snippet.title: Uttam Nagar Food Tour | Delhi Street Food | Veggie Paaji
snippet.description:
Join Veggie Paaji on an exciting food adventure in Uttam Nagar, West Delhi! In this latest episode of our Delhi Food Series, we're diving deep into the vibrant street food scene to uncover "Uttam Nagar Special" dishes, from unique momos to authentic dhaba-style meals.

Highlights of our culinary journey:

King's Momos: Indulge in crispy Kurkure Momos [01:59], flavorful Afghani Momos [02:40], spicy Tandoori Momos [02:40], and tender Tandoori Chaap [02:50]. Don't miss their delicious Dahi Bhalla [00:56]!

Location: King's Momos, Uttam Nagar

Bhagwandas Chole Tikki: Savor the classic combination of crispy Chole Tikki [09:41] with a spicy chickpea curry.

Location: Bhagwandas Chole Tikki, Uttam Nagar (This is a street vendor, so the precise location may vary, but it's on Arya Samaj Road).

Anand Vaishno Dhaba: Experience authentic North Indian cuisine with their rich Special Chana Masala [15:22], creamy Dal Makhni [15:24], and soft Butter Naan [15:25].

Location: Anand Vaishno Dhaba, Uttam Nagar

Scoops Ice Cream, Shakes & Mocktails: End your food tour with a refreshing Oreo Cone Softie [19:46] or a classic Vanilla Softie [19:59] at this 24/7 spot!

Location: Scoops, Uttam Nagar

Come along as we explore the best of Uttam Nagar's street food, offering genuine reviews and a taste of Delhi's incredible culinary diversity!

snippet.description:
Golden Fish Kitchen

In today’s video, we take you to the heart of Dombivli, where we discovered an absolute hidden gem — Golden Fish Kitchen, a humble street-side eatery run by a beautiful and hardworking couple. They serve authentic Agri-style seafood and non-veg delicacies that are bursting with coastal flavors and tradition.

We had the chance to try some of their best-selling dishes, including the Surmai Fish Fry, Pomfret Fry, Bombil Fry, and the rich, flavorful Prawns Curry. Each bite was a perfect blend of spice, crunch, and freshness. We also indulged in the unique Jawla Wadi and the spicy, lip-smacking Jawla Chutney, both of which added a rustic charm to the meal.

What truly sets this place apart is not just the food, but the love and dedication the couple pours into every dish. Their warmth and hospitality make the entire experience even more memorable.

If you’re a seafood or non-veg lover and want to explore the true taste of Agri cuisine, Golden Fish Kitchen is a must-visit. Don’t miss out on this flavorful journey through Dombivli’s street food scene!

snippet.title: Best Lucknow Brunch Food Tour : Sursuri / Bandook Chaat, Bun Chola, Bakse Wale Khaste, Malai Makhan
snippet.description:
Lucknow is often celebrated for its rich Awadhi cuisine, but the city also boasts a thriving vegetarian street food culture that deserves equal recognition. On this special food tour, we teamed up with Priyank, a passionate local food explorer, to experience a classic Lucknawi vegetarian brunch. Priyank, known for his insightful vlogs, guided us through some of the city's most beloved breakfast spots, offering a glimpse into its vibrant morning food scene.  

Our first stop was a small but iconic tea stall, M/S Ram Kewal Tea Stall, located on Maqbara Road in Hazratganj. A favorite among locals, this place serves a comforting cup of tea made by mixing tea liquor with milk. The tea was paired with bun makhan, generously slathered with unsalted white butter sourced from a local dairy. We also tried their samosa and sihal, a lesser-known but delicious deep-fried snack that complemented the tea perfectly.  

Next, we made our way to Gupta Ji Khaste Wale at Chowk Kotwali, Gol Darwaza, Chowk, where we tried a special breakfast dish called bakse wale khasta. These khasta kachoris are stored and served from metallic trunks, giving them their distinctive name. Accompanied by dry masala wale aalu, this dish is immensely popular, and the stock often runs out between 7 and 10 in the morning.  

At Gol Darwaza, Chowk, we visited Malai Makhan Corner to sample the quintessential winter delicacy, malai makhan. This creamy, airy sweet, infused with a subtle hint of cardamom, was a delightful experience. Many vendors sell it in this area, but the one we visited had recently hosted actor Diljit Dosanjh, further cementing its reputation.  

Moving ahead, we stopped at Sewak Ram Misthan Bhandar near Kalli Ji Ram Mandir in Sarrafa Bazaar, Chowk. This old sweet and snack shop is known for its traditional preparations made entirely in ghee. Here, we tried the poori and sabzi combo, a dish that evoked the flavors of food found in the holy cities of Uttar Pradesh. We also tasted jalebi dahi and two seasonal varieties of ladoo, each showcasing the richness of Lucknawi sweets.  

While heading to our next stop, we came across an intriguing roadside stall named Badnaam Chole Stall at Gwynne Road in Aminabad Market. True to its name, the stall had an element of curiosity around it. We tried their chole suhal and bun chole makhan, both offering a unique take on the classic chole preparation.  

Our final destination was Pandit Chaat Corner near Khun Khun Ji Jewellers in Aminabad. A hidden gem in the city’s bustling chaat scene, this place is known for its batashe, sursuri chaat, matar chaat, and a few other specialties. The owner, Kalyan ji, welcomed us warmly and treated us to a variety of dishes, each bursting with distinct flavors and textures. His hospitality and passion for food made the experience even more memorable.  

This food tour through Lucknow’s vegetarian delights offered a refreshing perspective on the city’s diverse culinary heritage. Each stop added a unique layer to our understanding of its street food culture, making it an experience worth savoring.

True to its name, the stall had an element of curiosity around it. We tried their chole suhal and bun chole makhan, both offering a unique take on the classic chole preparation.  

Our final destination was Pandit Chaat Corner near Khun Khun Ji Jewellers in Aminabad. A hidden gem in the city’s bustling chaat scene, this place is known for its batashe, sursuri chaat, matar chaat, and a few other specialties. The owner, Kalyan ji, welcomed us warmly and treated us to a variety of dishes, each bursting with distinct flavors and textures. His hospitality and passion for food made the experience even more memorable.  

This food tour through Lucknow’s vegetarian delights offered a refreshing perspective on the city’s diverse culinary heritage. Each stop added a unique layer to our understanding of its street food culture, making it an experience worth savoring.

snippet.title: MORADABAD Non Veg Food Tour I Biscuit Wali Gali + Shabnam Double Roti + Keeme ki Poori + HabshiHalwa
snippet.description:
Join us on an unforgettable Iftar Food Walk in Moradabad, where centuries-old culinary traditions blend seamlessly with the warmth of its people. Guided by our gracious host Sayeed Ahmed, we spent an evening exploring lanes filled with aromas, stories, and a deep sense of community during Ramzan.

Our journey began in the iconic Biscuit Wali Gali in Kath Ki Puliya, home to Shabnam Walon Ki Mehak Bread. This narrow bylane, famous for its baked goods, introduced us to the unique breads that become an essential part of iftar in Moradabad. From airy loaves to dense, flavour-packed varieties, each bread reflects a local tradition and a purpose on the Ramzan table.

We then headed to Baburam Misthan Bhandar in Bartan Bazaar, a legendary establishment that has been serving the city since 1891. Stepping inside felt like stepping back in time. Here we tasted their classic jalebi, rabri and khurchan, all prepared in pure desi ghee. Every bite reminded us why this shop still stands tall after more than a century, consistency, craft, and love.

The highlight of our walk was an intimate iftar at the home of Dr. Rafey Fahim and Dr. Anas Fahim. As conversations flowed, we learned about Moradabad’s traditions around sheri (pre-dawn meal). Their table was a reflection of the family’s love for food, aloo ki pakodi, samose, jalebi, chicken fry, fruit chaat, chole, keeme ki puri, biryani, zarda, bihari dishes, dahi phulki, and a fragrant homemade biryani. A feast rooted in personal preferences, nostalgic cravings, and Ramzan warmth. Being welcomed into their home was truly special.

Post a small breather, we resumed our food trail at Zaitoon, Lajpat Nagar, known for blending Middle Eastern flavours with local tastes. We savoured gola kebab, chicken tikka seasoned with sumac-thyme-basil, al fahm, and their popular parda biryani. The sight of freshly grilled kebabs and trays of festive sweets added yet another layer to our Ramzan experience.

A short stroll brought us to Haji Abdul Jabbar Dairy at Indra Chowk, a beloved Sheri Milk Point. Generations have stopped here for nourishing milk-based drinks that keep them energised through the fast. It’s places like this that hold the emotional weight of Ramzan memories.

From there, our walk continued to Salman Food Chicken Corner for their shawarma and khaboos, followed by Gulshan-e-Karim, a legendary Mughlai shop established in 1901. Here we watched fresh seekh kebabs come straight off the skewers, accompanied by timeless dishes that define Moradabad’s Mughlai identity.

At Rampur Sweets Corner, an 80-year-old establishment on Nai Sarak, we explored sweets that trace their origins to Rampur, katli, habsi halwa, angoor dana, and the unique aohan halwa. These sweets, prepared year-round, carry flavours not commonly found outside this region.

Kacheri Road welcomed us with two major stops. First, Mezban Shama Chicken Corner (est. 2007), where we tried their much-loved non-vegetarian delicacies, chicken seekh kebab, roomali roti, chicken korma, and tawa chicken. Each dish was bold, hearty, and unapologetically flavourful.

Then, The Pahelwan Food, where Zaheer took us through their menu and family legacy. His father, a pehelwan, crafted many of the recipes still used today. Since 1983, this shop has been known for its rich use of ghee and their signature roasted chicken, a dish that carries generations of expertise.

We ended the night with a comforting cup of tea, the perfect wrap to a long, flavour-packed walk through Moradabad’s lanes.

This episode isn’t just about food, it’s about people opening their hearts, preserving traditions, and sharing their Ramzan with us. Step into the spirit of Moradabad and experience its iftar culture, one delicious stop at a time.

snippet.title: Kasol to Manali Via Naggar Food Trip | Naggar Castle Bakery Rum ball + Cheese Spinach/Kothey Momo
snippet.description:
After spending a peaceful day in Kasol, we set off for Manali the next morning with our gracious host Khushboo, for whom Himachal truly feels like a second home. We began our day with breakfast at Kailasha - The Himalayan Village. It was raining gently, and the meal felt soulful and comforting. The spread included assorted fruits, garlic bread, dalia pulao, idli, and coffee - all homestyle and served in a serene setting.
On our way to Manali, we made a quick stop at Naggar Castle, a popular and historic site known for its beautiful wood and stone architecture and panoramic views of the valley. Just nearby, we stumbled upon a charming homemade bakery that’s a hit with tourists. Their rum ball and carrot cake are quick to sell out – and we were lucky to get our hands on them.
Not long after, we noticed a makeshift honey stall along the road. The owner explained how honey is cultivated using artificial hives inside boxes, which are later processed and reused. We tasted three types of honey, each one unique in flavor.
We then reached Sunbloom Cafe and met its passionate owner who shared the journey of how this scenic cafe came into being. The outdoor seating was inviting and peaceful. We enjoyed fresh juice and delicious spinach momos before continuing on.
By the time we arrived in Manali, it was evening and we were hungry. We kept dinner simple - comforting dal roti at Beas Punjabi Dhaba. A satisfying end to a day full of scenic views, and soulful food.
